Slides and video recording of the webinar given by Rita Gautschy (DaSCH) and Auriane Marmier (FORS) on May 28, 2025, part of the FORS-DaSCH series on data management for the social sciences and humanities. The webinar explains why consistent naming and description make research information retrievable and interoperable. It introduces authority data (e.g. GND, VIAF, ORCID, Wikidata, Getty AAT, GeoNames) and how it helps to disambiguate entities and link data. It then presents two key standards in the humanities: IIIF for images (Image and Presentation APIs, with emerging 3D support) and TEI for encoding texts. From the social sciences side, it covers descriptive, structural and administrative metadata, the difference between metadata and documentation, the DDI standard, and controlled vocabularies such as ELSST, ISCED and ISCO. It ends by comparing how the two disciplines use these tools.

## Learning outcomes

After working through this resource, users will be able to:

- define authority data and name the main authority files for people, places, subjects and works
- explain the purpose of IIIF and TEI and how they support interoperability
- distinguish types of metadata and the difference between metadata and documentation
- find and choose suitable metadata standards and controlled vocabularies (e.g. DDI, ELSST, BARTOC)
